\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Invariance — Taylor}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.Taylor
\section{Overview}
Cubic Taylor approximation with an explicit fourth-order remainder gives integrability and scalar replacement estimates for the invariance moment conditions.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth-order Taylor remainder bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_sub_taylor_cubic_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_sub_taylor_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be four times continuously differentiable, and
suppose $C\ge0$ and $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. For all
$a,b\in\mathbb R$,
\[\left|\psi(a+b)-\sum_{j=0}^{3}\frac{\psi^{(j)}(a)}{j!}b^j\right|\le\frac{C}{24}b^4.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integrability under fourth moment control]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_test_of_memLp_four}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_test_of_memLp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $Z:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ belong to
$L^4(\mu)$, and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be four times continuously
differentiable. If $C\ge 0$ and $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$, then
$\omega\mapsto\psi(Z(\omega))$ is integrable under $\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cubic Taylor polynomial under matched moments]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_taylor_cubic}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_taylor_polynomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $\mathbb E
X=0$, $\mathbb E X^2=1$, $\mathbb E X^3=0$, and $\mathbb E X^4\le 9$, and suppose $X$ is
measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment. For every function
$\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, the expectation of
$\sum_{j=0}^{3}\frac{\psi^{(j)}(a)}{j!}(bX)^j$ is $\psi(a)+\frac{\psi^{(2)}(a)}{2}b^2$,
where the derivatives are iterated derivatives.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected scalar Taylor error]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_sub_taylor_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_sub_taylor_polynomial_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_taylor_cubic}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ satisfy the
fourth-order invariance moment conditions: it has finite fourth absolute moment, and its
first, second, and third moments are $0,1,0$, respectively, with fourth moment at most
$9$. Let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be four times continuously differentiable, and
suppose $C\ge0$ and $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. Then for all
$a,b\in\mathbb R$,
\[\left|\int_\Omega\psi(a+bX(\omega))\,d\mu(\omega)-\left(\psi(a)+\frac{\psi''(a)}2b^2\right)\right|\le\frac{3C}{8}b^4.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Comparison of scalar affine input laws]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.affine_replacement_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_sub_taylor_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability spaces, and let
$X\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $Y\colon\Xi\to\mathbb R$ each satisfy the fourth-order
invariance moment conditions: they are measurable up to null sets with finite fourth
absolute moments, have means zero, second moments one, third moments zero, and fourth
moments at most $9$. Let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be four times continuously
differentiable, and suppose $C\ge0$ and $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for every real $t$. For
all $a,b\in\mathbb R$,
\[\left|\mathbb E_\mu[\psi(a+bX)]-\mathbb E_\nu[\psi(a+bY)]\right|\le\frac{3C}{4}b^4.\]
\end{theorem}

\section{Additional declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Taylor remainder bound of arbitrary order]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_sub_taylor_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_sub_taylor_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $m\ge0$ be an integer, let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $(m+1)$ times
continuously differentiable, and suppose $C\in\mathbb R$ satisfies $|\psi^{(m+1)}(t)|\le
C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. For all $a,b\in\mathbb R$,
\[\left|\psi(a+b)-\sum_{j=0}^{m}\frac{\psi^{(j)}(a)}{j!}b^j\right|\le\frac{C}{(m+1)!}|b|^{m+1}.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integrability of a smooth function of a random variable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_test_of_memLp}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_test_of_memLp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_sub_taylor_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrable_mul_pow_of_memLp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, and let
$Z:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ belong to $L^{m+1}(\mu)$. Let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be
$(m+1)$-times continuously differentiable, and suppose there is a real number $C$ such
that $|\psi^{(m+1)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. Then
$\omega\mapsto\psi(Z(\omega))$ is integrable under $\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integration of a Taylor polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_taylor_polynomial}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_taylor_polynomial}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrable_mul_pow_of_memLp}
\difficulty{3}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $p,m\in\mathbb N$, and let
$X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have finite $p$th moment, with $m\le p$. For every function
$\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $\int
\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\frac{\psi^{(j)}(a)}{j!}(bX)^j\,d\mu=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\frac{\psi^{(j)}(a)}{j!}b^j\int
X^j\,d\mu$, where $\psi^{(j)}$ denotes the $j$th iterated derivative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected Taylor polynomial error]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_sub_taylor_polynomial_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_sub_taylor_polynomial_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_sub_taylor_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_test_of_memLp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrable_mul_pow_of_memLp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $m\in\mathbb N$, and let
$X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have finite $(m+1)$st absolute moment. Let $\psi:\mathbb
R\to\mathbb R$ be $(m+1)$ times continuously differentiable, and suppose $C\in\mathbb R$
satisfies $|\psi^{(m+1)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. For all $a,b\in\mathbb R$,
\[\left|\int_\Omega\psi(a+bX(\omega))\,d\mu(\omega)-\int_\Omega\sum_{j=0}^{m}\frac{\psi^{(j)}(a)}{j!}(bX(\omega))^j\,d\mu(\omega)\right|\le\frac{C}{(m+1)!}|b|^{m+1}\int_\Omega|X(\omega)|^{m+1}\,d\mu(\omega).\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Third-order affine replacement bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.affine_replacement_bound_c3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.affine_replacement_bound_c3}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_sub_taylor_polynomial_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_taylor_polynomial}
\difficulty{5}
For probability spaces $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$, and let
$X\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $Y\colon\Xi\to\mathbb R$ have finite third absolute
moments. Suppose their means and second moments agree. Let $\psi\colon\mathbb
R\to\mathbb R$ be three times continuously differentiable, and suppose
$|\psi^{(3)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. Then, for all $a,b\in\mathbb R$,
\[
\left|\int \psi(a+bX)\,d\mu-\int \psi(a+bY)\,d\nu\right|
\le \frac C6 |b|^3\left(\int |X|^3\,d\mu+\int |Y|^3\,d\nu\right).
\]
\end{theorem}
